entities.summary:
Harald Bluetooth was a king of Denmark and Norway, who ruled from approximately 940 to 986. He is best known for his efforts to unify the warring factions in Denmark under a single ruler. 

 Born into the Gormsson dynasty, Harald Bluetooth succeeded his half-brother Gorm the Old as King of Denmark around 940. Through strategic alliances and military conquests, he expanded his kingdom's borders and solidified its position as a major power in Scandinavia. 

 One of Harald Bluetooth's most significant achievements was his unification of Denmark and Norway under a single ruler, creating the Kingdom of Denmark and Norway. This marked a turning point in Scandinavian history, as it paved the way for future kingdoms and empires to rise in the region.

 Harald Bluetooth also played a crucial role in the spread of Christianity throughout Scandinavia. He was baptized into the Christian faith by the Viking missionary Rollo, who later became the Duke of Normandy. 

 Despite his significant achievements, Harald Bluetooth's reign was cut short when he died on November 6, 986. His legacy lived on, however, as he became a legendary figure in Scandinavian folklore and history.

 In recent years, researchers have uncovered evidence of Harald Bluetooth's involvement in the development of the firstBluetooth technology, which revolutionized wireless communication.
